title: URBAN FLOOD RISK MITIGATION PROGRAMME
body_text:
The Central Government has approved Urban Flood Risk Management Programme (UFRMP) Phase-I in seven (07) cities viz. Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Mumbai and Pune at a total financial outlay of Rs. 3075.65 crore and has also approved UFRMP Phase-II in eleven (11) cities viz. Bhopal, Bhubaneshwar, Guwahati, Jaipur, Kanpur, Patna, Raipur, Trivandrum, Vishakhapatnam, Indore and Lucknow at a total financial outlay of Rs. 2444.42 crore for financial assistance under National Disaster Mitigation Fund (NDMF). The State-wise details of fund allocated and released under UFRMP Phase-I and UFRMP Phase-II are at Annexure.
The projects approved by the Central Government under UFRMP are being implemented by the concerned State Governments. The approved projects for all 07 cities under UFRMP Phase-I and for Guwahati under UFRMP Phase-II are at various stages of implementation. The projects being implemented under UFRMP are expected to significantly improve stormwater conveyance, reduce flooding and waterlogging, enhance road connectivity, and increase the resilience of the drainage network in the cities. However, a final city-wise assessment of outcome can be undertaken after adequate implementation. To review the progress of implementation of projects under UFRMP and to ensure timely completion of the projects, periodic meetings are held at Ministry of Home Affairs and National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA). NDMA has also prepared a Monitoring and Evaluation Framework for UFRMP and has circulated the same to participating cities for adoption and reporting.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs informed the Lok Sabha that the Union Government has approved the Urban Flood Risk Management Programme (UFRMP) in two phases: Phase-I covering 7 cities (Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Mumbai, Pune) with an outlay of Rs 3075.65 crore, and Phase-II covering 11 cities (Bhopal, Bhubaneshwar, Guwahati, Jaipur, Kanpur, Patna, Raipur, Trivandrum, Vishakhapatnam, Indore, Lucknow) with an outlay of Rs 2444.42 crore, funded under the National Disaster Mitigation Fund (NDMF). All Phase-I city projects and Guwahati under Phase-II are under implementation, aimed at improving stormwater drainage and urban flood resilience, with NDMA monitoring progress via a Monitoring and Evaluation Framework.
enrichment.context:
Urban flooding has become a recurring disaster risk in India due to rapid, often unplanned urbanization, encroachment on natural drainage channels and wetlands, inadequate stormwater infrastructure, and climate-change-induced intense rainfall events, as seen in Chennai (2015), Mumbai (2005, 2017), Bengaluru (2022) and Hyderabad. The National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), under the Disaster Management Act, 2005, has increasingly emphasized mitigation and structural interventions rather than only post-disaster response. The National Disaster Mitigation Fund (NDMF), constituted under Section 47 of the DM Act, finances such structural and non-structural mitigation projects, distinct from the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) which funds relief after disasters occur.

The UFRMP represents a shift toward proactive, city-specific mitigation planning by targeting India's major metros and state capitals prone to waterlogging, focusing on augmenting stormwater conveyance systems, desilting drains, and improving drainage network resilience. The phased approach (Phase-I for large metros, Phase-II extending to state capitals and Tier-II cities) reflects an attempt to institutionalize urban flood resilience nationwide. Centre-State cooperative federalism is central here, as implementation rests with State Governments while funding and monitoring are coordinated by MHA/NDMA, highlighting persistent governance challenges around fund utilization, as seen in the low fund release for most Phase-II cities.

prelims_questions.question: The Urban Flood Risk Management Programme (UFRMP) mentioned in news is funded through which of the following?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that UFRMP Phase-I and Phase-II are approved for financial assistance under the National Disaster Mitigation Fund (NDMF), which is distinct from the response-oriented NDRF/SDRF.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following cities is included under UFRMP Phase-I?
prelims_questions.explanation: Chennai is one of the seven cities under UFRMP Phase-I (along with Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Mumbai, Pune); Guwahati, Jaipur and Lucknow are Phase-II cities.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the causes of recurrent urban flooding in Indian metropolitan cities and evaluate the effectiveness of central government mitigation programmes like the Urban Flood Risk Management Programme (UFRMP) in addressing them.
Examine the institutional and financial architecture of disaster mitigation in India, distinguishing between mitigation and response funds, with reference to recent urban infrastructure programmes.
